claims.text: The initial alloy is equal-atomic NbMoTaW.
The as-cast NbMoTaW alloy is single-phase BCC.
Controlled annealing followed by optimized cooling can modify the microstructure of equal-atomic NbMoTaW.
The proposed treatment can enhance room-temperature ductility.
The proposed treatment can preserve high-temperature mechanical performance.
The proposed treatment can preserve irradiation resistance.
Intermediate-temperature annealing and controlled cooling can produce a refined grain structure and beneficial grain-boundary characteristics.
Preserving the single-phase BCC structure requires subcritical annealing and controlled cooling that avoid deleterious precipitation or over-aging.
The treatment will enhance grain-boundary character distribution and may form optimized grain-size substructures or twin boundaries.
The proposed grain-boundary features and substructures facilitate dislocation movement.
Controlled annealing reduces residual stresses.
Controlled annealing creates a uniform grain structure that eases room-temperature dislocation motion.
Easier room-temperature dislocation motion improves ductility.
Preservation of the BCC phase and its high-temperature stability will keep high-temperature strength unaffected.
Preservation of the BCC phase and its high-temperature stability will keep irradiation resistance unaffected.
Untreated equal-atomic NbMoTaW has limited room-temperature ductility.
Untreated equal-atomic NbMoTaW has excellent high-temperature mechanical properties.
Untreated equal-atomic NbMoTaW has predicted irradiation resistance.
Excessively high annealing temperatures or unsuitable cooling rates can cause unwanted precipitation or grain coarsening.
Unwanted precipitation or grain coarsening may compromise high-temperature strength or irradiation resistance.
